title: Beyond-diffusion control for the crawler's cargo containment: a uniformly slower cargo (D/4, D/10, no layer exclusion) is left behind just the same (rear in/out 0.92-1.03 vs 3.4-3.8 with the layer)
summary: Matched Laplacian-only twin for W in 20261026T0243-c31-crawler-layer-repair-claim: the claim world (research/alife/collective/contrib/20261026T0243-c31-crawler-layer-repair-claim/world.py, run here as cargoprobe.py on the identical world3) with the layer's exclusion off (kappa=0) and the cargo's diffusivity lowered uniformly from 0.05 to 0.0125 and 0.005, seeds 0 and 2, t=0-12 (the cell trajectory is identical in every arm, since neither s nor c feeds back). Over t=1-8 the in/out ratio by signed distance is ~2 in every plain-diffusion arm only because the front advances onto clean ground; on the rear side it is 0.95-1.16 at D, 0.95-1.03 at D/4 and 0.92-0.99 at D/10, and the cell holds 42-44% of its cargo, against rear 3.4-3.8 and 70% with kappa=10 at D=0.05 (bdtable.txt, bd_cmp.png). Lowering D makes containment slightly worse, not better: a slower cargo stays where it was made and the retracting rear passes over it. So no uniform diffusivity reproduces the containment; it needs the layer to sweep the cargo, which only an interface-bound exclusion does.

finding.operator: exclusion of the cargo by the cell's own adsorbed layer (cargo potential ln c + kappa s) vs uniformly lowered cargo diffusivity
finding.control: matched Laplacian-only twin: kappa=0 with Dc = 0.05, 0.0125, 0.005 on seeds 0 and 2
